title: gridsearch-latency-cost-quality-heuristic-notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the grid-search style experiments we ran for onboarding the new LlamaX-30B-quant candidate into the hosted inference fleet. Focus is on practical heuristics for trading latency vs token-cost vs quality for real prompt sets (chatty multi-turn + single-turn completions). The aim: produce a short set of rules that SRE, serving, and product teams can use to pick defaults and regression thresholds for canary rollouts.

Background & motivation:
- Prior onboarding attempts bumped tail latency under load due to batching interactions with KV cache behavior; cost per 1k tokens also rose unexpectedly when max_tokens defaults were increased for some prompt sets.
- We want to codify an experiment pattern to expose those tradeoffs reproducibly: a 3-D sweep across batch_size, cache_enabled, and max_tokens with per-prompt-type buckets.

Experiment overview:
- Model: LlamaX-30B-quant (candidate); baseline is LlamaV2-13B-optim (production).
- Hardware: Dedicated p4d-like nodes (8xA100-80GB equivalent) and a representative n1-standard serving cluster using smaller GPUs for hosted mode. Primary numbers in this doc are from the p4d-like nodes.
- Prompt sets: three curated eval sets representing customer workloads:
  1) multi-turn-assistant (MT): 1.2k samples, average historical seq length = 420 tokens; high context reuse (prefix common across samples).
  2) short-completions (SC): 2.5k samples, avg seq = 64 tokens; latency-sensitive.
  3) retrieval-augmented (RA): 800 samples, avg seq = 380 tokens, contains repeated retrieval tokens leading to KV cache hits when enabled.
- Sweep dims: batch_size ∈ {1,2,4,8,16}; cache_enabled ∈ {true,false}; max_tokens ∈ {64,128,256,512}.
- Workload shape: steady-state qps ramp to target that saturates GPU compute while preserving ~20% headroom to trigger batching effects (approx 250 qps for p4d-like cluster for candidate).
- Metrics collected per config and per prompt-set: p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, median_tokens_per_request, cost_per_1k_generated_tokens (USD, modeled using internal cost model), semantic_quality (mean embedding-similarity vs reference, normalized 0-1), pass_rate (task-specific accuracy for MT testcases), KV_cache_hit_rate (when cache_enabled true), and GPU_utilization_percent.

Selected raw results (aggregated highlights):
- Short-completions (SC):
  * batch=1, cache=false, max_tokens=64 -> p95=82ms, p50=34ms, cost_per_1k=0.42, quality=0.86
  * batch=8, cache=false, max_tokens=64 -> p95=210ms, p50=120ms, cost_per_1k=0.29, quality=0.86
  * batch=8, cache=true, max_tokens=64 -> p95=160ms, p50=95ms, cost_per_1k=0.22, quality=0.86, kv_hit=0.12
  Observation: batching reduces cost but increases tail latency; enabling KV cache recovers some tail latency while preserving cost wins.

- Multi-turn (MT):
  * batch=1, cache=false, max_tokens=256 -> p95=420ms, p50=210ms, cost_per_1k=1.12, quality=0.78
  * batch=4, cache=true, max_tokens=256 -> p95=480ms, p50=260ms, cost_per_1k=0.72, quality=0.78, kv_hit=0.45
  * batch=16, cache=true, max_tokens=256 -> p95=680ms, p50=410ms, cost_per_1k=0.63, quality=0.78, kv_hit=0.45
  Observation: for long-context MT, cache brings big cost wins and preserves quality; tail latency remains sensitive to batch size because longer sequence lengths magnify queueing.

- Retrieval-augmented (RA):
  * batch=2, cache=true, max_tokens=512 -> p95=610ms, p50=350ms, cost_per_1k=1.38, quality=0.90, kv_hit=0.62
  * batch=8, cache=false, max_tokens=512 -> p95=980ms, p50=520ms, cost_per_1k=1.01, quality=0.90
  Observation: RA shows the largest KV benefit (expected); disabling cache increases both cost and tail latency due to reprocessing long retrieval prefixes.

Cross-cutting insights:
1) Cost vs latency convexity: For most prompt-sets, increasing batch size from 1->4 yields large cost reductions with modest p95 increases. Past batch=8, tail latency increases superlinearly for MT/RA sets.
2) Cache is a net win when prefix reuse > ~15% and average context length > ~200 tokens. We estimated a simple break-even: cost_with_cache ≈ cost_no_cache * (1 - kv_hit_rate * cache_efficiency); with measured cache_efficiency ~0.7 on candidate runs.
3) max_tokens has linear impact on cost and near-linear impact on p95 for long contexts (because worst-case sequence length influences kernel selection and KV handling). For SC set, increasing max_tokens from 64->128 increased cost ~18% but p95 increased only ~10%; for MT and RA the increases were larger.
4) Quality is remarkably stable across batch/cache variations for this model on these prompt-sets (<1-2% absolute change in embedding-sim similarity or pass rates). However, quantization artifacts of the 30B-quant candidate show tiny degradations for very short prompts (SC) when max_tokens is large — likely sampling/temperature interaction at tail tokens.

Operational heuristics (practical rules for defaults):
- Latency-sensitive (p95 SLO <= 200ms): use batch_size=1 or 2, cache=true if prefix reuse predictable; cap max_tokens=64 for SC-like routes.
- Cost-sensitive (minimize USD/token with p95 up to ~500ms allowed): batch_size=4, cache=true, max_tokens tuned to 128/256 depending on median seq length.
- High-quality long-context (MT/RA with required semantic fidelity): cache=true mandatory, batch_size<=8; prefer max_tokens based on 95th percentile seq length observed in telemetry.
- Canary defaults for LlamaX-30B-quant: start with batch=4, cache=true, max_tokens=256 for Dedicated trials; monitor p95 and kv_hit_rate in first 48h.

Regression detection guidance for CI/canary pipelines:
- Track per-prompt-set deltas vs baseline for these signals over rolling-1h windows during canary: p95_latency, cost_per_minute, semantic_quality. Alert if:
  * p95 increases by > 30% and absolute p95 exceeds 500ms for any MT/RA route, OR
  * cost_per_1k increases by > 25% without quality gain, OR
  * semantic_quality drops by > 3% absolute.
- Break down alerts by batch size / cache flag to help triage: a regression that only appears when cache_enabled=true suggests model runtime mismatch in KV handling.

Notes on experiment artifacts and reproducibility:
- Raw logs and per-request traces are in the experiment bucket: s3://redwood-experiments/lx-30b-gridsearch/ (linked in Jira -> JIRA-ML-889).
- Synthetic load generator: git ref runtime/perf/loadgen@c3f5b8 (attached PR 756). Use the provided seed files to reproduce exact sequence length distributions.
- We ported a small script (scripts/compute_cost_model.py) to estimate USD/token under different reserved capacity amortizations — see linked PR.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Dynamic batching policies: can we implement a latency-aware batching threshold that keeps batch>1 when CPU latency predicts safe p95? Early tests show potential to capture cost wins while bounding p95, but implementation risk remains.
- Cache TTL / contamination: RA set showed kv_hit_rate decay over long runs when mixing many retrieval contexts. Need to prototype per-route cache partitioning or small LRU TTLs to avoid contamination.
- Model-specific quantization behaviors: run a targeted short-prompt sweep with temperature=0.0 to isolate quantization vs sampling issues seen in SC when max_tokens is large.

Recommendations (next steps):
1) Canary rollout: LlamaX-30B-quant on Dedicated with default batch=4, cache=true, max_tokens=256 for 72h with strict alerting rules (see Regression detection guidance).
2) Implement quick telemetry dashboards: p95 by route, kv_hit_rate, cost_per_minute, and distribution of seq lengths observed in production to auto-suggest max_tokens per route.
3) Prototype latency-aware dynamic batching in a staging cluster; aim for a soft bound on batch-size growth tied to predicted p95.

Appendix (short checklist for handoff to SRE and product):
- [ ] Add canary job with the config above and include JIRA-ML-889 in the rollout notes.
- [ ] Wire alerts for the three regression rules to #ml-onboard-alerts with runbook links.
- [ ] Add per-route seq-length histogram ingestion into observability for 30 days.
